title: AI Facebook Ad Generator for Online Stores | AIVideosUGC
description: Try an AI Facebook ad generator made for sellers: turn one product photo into a short clip or square product visual, then add your offer in Ads Manager.
h1: AI Facebook Ad Generator for Square and Vertical Ads
lead: Use this AI Facebook ad generator to make a square product image or a 9:16 Reels clip from one photo, then write the headline and offer in Ads Manager.
card: Square product images and 9:16 Reels clips.
intro: Facebook campaigns can reach people in Feed, Stories and Reels as they browse posts from friends and groups. A clear look at the product helps the creative read quickly. Meta recommends 4:5 (1440×1800) images and video for Feed; AIVideosUGC makes 6, 10 or 15-second clips and square product images from one photo, which you crop to 4:5 for Feed, and 9:16 clips for Reels, keeping key details inside the safe area.

It fits store owners who run their own campaigns and need something new to try without a photoshoot. Describe the scene you want, such as a lunch box packed on a kitchen counter or a dog harness on a morning walk, and check the credit cost before you start. Your headline, price and button text belong in Ads Manager, where they stay easy to edit. Plan one scene for each placement: a 4:5 Feed product ad, a tall Stories frame with breathing room, a 9:16 Reels explanation, or a catalog retargeting view that puts the same product in a new setting.
specs: Square output; crop to 4:5 before you upload
tips: Check that the product and any key wording still make sense with the sound off.
Keep any words on the visual short, and put the details in the primary text and headline fields in Ads Manager.
Crop square images to 4:5 for Feed and prepare 9:16 clips for Reels as separate jobs, then check the placement preview in Ads Manager.

ideas.d: For an organizer or storage bin, describe the cluttered space first and the neat result after, in one 10- or 15-second clip.
A square image of the product beside wrapping paper and a ribbon, ready for gift-season ads.
A clean lifestyle shot of a product people already looked at on your site, for ads aimed at past visitors.

faq.q: How can I check a Facebook ad before it runs?
faq.a: Open the Feed, Stories, and Reels previews separately and check that product details stay clear of buttons, captions, and profile controls.

faq.q: Can AIVideosUGC run my Facebook campaign?
faq.a: No. We make the video or image; you download it and set up the budget, audience and schedule in Ads Manager.

faq.q: Can I make several versions to test against each other?
faq.a: Yes, one at a time. Each version shows its own credit cost before you start, and you can compare how they perform in Ads Manager.

faq.q: Will Facebook reject an ad because it was made with AI?
faq.a: Meta reviews each ad under its current Advertising Standards. Review claims, rights, and any AI-label requirement in Ads Manager before launch.

faq.q: Which format should I use for Feed or Reels?
faq.a: Meta recommends 4:5 (1440×1800) for Feed images and video and 9:16 for Reels. AIVideosUGC outputs square stills you can crop to 4:5 before upload; make a separate 9:16 clip for Reels, then check each placement preview.

faq.q: Where do I add the headline and offer?
faq.a: Add the primary text, headline, price, code and call to action in Ads Manager after download so you can edit them for each campaign.

overview.d: A Facebook feed ad may be encountered while the viewer's sound is off. Build the visual around one unmistakable action: open the container, attach the clip, turn the dial, or place the item where it is used. Use the source photo to keep the product's shape and color anchored, then write the headline and offer in Ads Manager where you can revise them.

overview.h2: Choose a shape for each Meta placement
overview.d: Meta recommends 4:5 (1440×1800) creative for Feed and 9:16 video for Reels, with key messages inside the Reels safe area. AIVideosUGC outputs square stills to crop to 4:5 and 6, 10 or 15-second clips; run the 9:16 shape for Reels as a separate job and check each placement preview.

overview.h2: Build one version for Feed and one for Reels
overview.d: Feed and Reels place controls in different parts of the screen. Keep the product and the first action clear in the 4:5 Feed crop, then run a separate 9:16 version for Reels when the tall framing changes the composition. Use the placement preview in Ads Manager to check the image crop, headline truncation, button area, and any safe-zone overlap before you publish.

overview.h2: Use the visual to support the offer
overview.d: A useful Facebook creative answers one question quickly: what is it, how is it used, or what changes after use? Show a lunch box being packed, a pet brush touching a coat, or a bottle pouring into a glass. Keep claims modest and verifiable. Put the price, discount code, primary text, headline, and call to action in Ads Manager so each audience can receive the right version.

overview.h2: Test the same message across placements
overview.d: Keep the product, offer, and audience constant when comparing a Feed image with a Reels clip. Change the crop or opening action only when the placement requires it. Name files with the placement and date, preview them with sound off, and confirm the product remains complete after Meta applies its automatic placement crop.

overview.h2: Leave room for the Feed crop
overview.d: A square still can be cropped before it becomes a 4:5 Feed asset, so keep the bottle, label area, and hand action away from the outer edge. Check the 1440×1800 preview after cropping and move any final price or code into Ads Manager. Reels gets its own 9:16 file when the taller framing would cut the product.

overview.h2: Map one product scene to each Meta placement
overview.d: Use the Feed product-ad frame for a 4:5 proof shot, Stories for a tall single action, Reels for a face-to-camera explanation, and catalog retargeting for the same product in a new setting. Keep the product and offer consistent, then add headline, price and button text in Ads Manager.

items.d: Use a front or three-quarter photo where the useful parts are visible, such as a latch, handle, control, or opening.
Choose a movement that communicates through the picture alone. A hand placing or using the product works better than an explanation that would need narration.
Keep the important object away from corners and lower controls so you can add a headline without hiding the product.

results.h2: What a useful Facebook asset contains

items.d: The item and its use should be apparent before the viewer reaches the end of a short clip.
Keep one square feed image and make a vertical video when Stories or Reels need a taller composition.
Leave the generated scene free of the exact price and code; place those in Ads Manager or an editor.

Square still photo of adult hands placing cut fruit into a reusable lunch box with visible compartments on a bright kitchen counter. Keep the lid open and the food neatly arranged in clean morning light.
Square still photo of an adult clipping a plain harness onto a calm dog beside a bright front doorway. Show the buckle and harness fit clearly in natural morning light; keep the dog relaxed.
Square still photo under a home-office desk: adult hands guide two loose cords into a compact cable tray fixed beneath the tabletop. Show the tidy channel and tray in soft window light.
Square still photo of adult hands lifting a plain gift-box lid to reveal a matching product set nestled in cream tissue on a bright dining table. Keep the full set centered in warm window light.

after_download.h2: Set up the ad in Ads Manager

items.d: Write the primary text, headline, price, code, and call to action in Ads Manager so each version stays easy to edit.
Add a licensed track in Ads Manager or an editor after download; AIVideosUGC does not add voiceover, music, or captions.
Check feed, Stories, and Reels previews separately. Move added text if a profile control, button, or caption covers it.
If you make several creatives, alter one opening or scene at a time and keep the audience and offer consistent for a readable comparison.

good: Products whose use can be understood visually
Stores that manage their own campaigns in Ads Manager
Catalogs needing both square feed and vertical placement assets
Promotions where the offer changes after the scene is made
not_ideal: Ads that require a spoken explanation to make sense
Claims or fine print that must be rendered inside the generated frame
